definition: Problem solving identifies a gap or obstacle, develops possible responses and evaluates whether a chosen solution works.
example: A support team compares explanations for delivery errors and tests the most likely cause.

definition: Process hazard analysis systematically examines what could go wrong in a process and evaluates potential consequences and safeguards.
example: A team reviews a proposed facility change to identify hazards requiring further controls.

definition: Process improvement measures how work performs and changes steps or conditions to achieve better results.
example: A team removes redundant approval steps and checks whether turnaround time improves.

definition: Process management defines, coordinates, monitors and maintains how recurring work is performed.
example: A supervisor assigns owners and checks whether cases move through each required stage.

definition: Process piping is the design, installation or maintenance of piping that conveys fluids used in an industrial process.
example: A designer specifies an appropriate piping layout for moving material between vessels.
sense_note: The label may denote the system itself or the associated work discipline.

definition: Processing.js was a JavaScript implementation for running Processing-style graphics programs in a web browser.
example: An artist used it to display an interactive drawing on a webpage.
sense_note: Distinguish it from the Processing desktop environment and p5.js.

definition: Procore is a construction management platform for coordinating project information, work and participants.
example: A contractor uses it to track requests for information and project documents.

definition: Product analysis evaluates a product's characteristics, performance or market fit to inform decisions.
example: A team compares proposed features with customer needs and development constraints.

definition: Product analytics uses behavioral and product data to understand how people use a product and where outcomes can improve.
example: A team analyzes which step of onboarding accounts for the most abandonment.

definition: Product benchmarking compares a product against other offerings or defined standards using consistent criteria.
example: A reviewer measures battery life across comparable devices using the same test conditions.

definition: Product catalogue management maintains the accuracy, structure and distribution of records describing products and offerings.
example: A catalog manager updates product dimensions and propagates the approved values to storefronts.

definition: Product leadership coordinates teams and decisions around product goals, priorities and delivery.
example: A product leader aligns engineering and design on which customer problem to address first.

definition: Product quality assurance establishes and applies practices that help ensure products meet requirements and reduce defects.
example: A team defines acceptance criteria and reviews defect patterns before release.

definition: Product requirements documentation records what a product or change must do, for whom, and under what constraints or acceptance conditions.
example: A product manager writes measurable criteria for a returns workflow.

definition: Product strategy decides which users and problems a product will serve and how it will achieve and sustain its intended outcomes.
example: A team focuses its roadmap on reducing onboarding costs for small organizations.

definition: Production support maintains the operation of deployed systems through monitoring, incident response and service recovery.
example: A support engineer investigates why an application stopped processing scheduled work.
sense_note: The wording may also refer to supporting a manufacturing line.

definition: Productivity management measures and improves how effectively time and resources are converted into useful outputs.
example: A manager adjusts how work is assigned after measuring bottlenecks and rework.

definition: Professionalism applies the conduct, reliability, ethical judgment and communication expected in a work setting.
example: A team member discloses a conflict of interest before participating in a purchasing decision.

definition: Profitability management monitors and improves the relationship between revenues and costs across activities or offerings.
example: A manager compares contribution margins before deciding whether to change a service package.

definition: Program evaluation systematically assesses a program's implementation, effectiveness or other outcomes against explicit questions and criteria.
example: An evaluator studies whether a tutoring program reached its intended students and improved attendance.

definition: Program optimization changes software to improve resource use or performance while preserving required behavior.
example: A developer profiles a slow report and rewrites the operation that dominates its runtime.
sense_note: The likely sense is computer-program optimization; in management it can mean improving program performance.

definition: Programmatic media buying uses software to automate the selection and purchase of advertising placements.
example: A campaign automatically bids for suitable ad impressions subject to its budget and targeting rules.

definition: Programmer's Hierarchical Interactive Graphics System is a standard interface for creating and manipulating structured, interactive computer graphics.
example: An application builds a hierarchy of graphic objects that can be edited and transformed as groups.

definition: Project benchmarking compares a project's practices or metrics with suitable references to identify differences and improvement opportunities.
example: A team compares its construction lead times with those of projects using similar scope and constraints.

definition: Project management plans, coordinates and controls resources and work to deliver a defined outcome within project constraints.
example: A project manager tracks dependencies and resolves a schedule conflict before it delays delivery.

definition: Project scoping defines a project's objectives, included and excluded work, deliverables, boundaries and constraints.
example: A team specifies that the first release will migrate current records but not archived records.

definition: Project status reporting communicates progress, risks, decisions and expected outcomes relative to a project plan.
example: A project lead reports which milestones are complete and flags a dependency threatening the next one.

definition: Prometheus is an open-source monitoring system that collects time-series metrics and supports queries and alerting rules.
example: An engineer sets an alert for sustained error rates above the service target.

definition: Prompt engineering designs and evaluates inputs and instructions to improve a model's responses for a specified task.
example: A developer tests whether a prompt with examples improves extraction accuracy on held-out documents.

definition: Proofreading checks a near-final text for errors in spelling, punctuation, grammar and presentation consistency.
example: An editor catches a misspelled name and inconsistent numbering before publication.

definition: Proposal development analyzes a request and produces a written offer explaining the proposed approach, costs and evidence of capability.
example: A team drafts a technical plan and budget in response to a request for proposals.

definition: Proposal management coordinates contributors, requirements, reviews and deadlines for preparing and submitting a proposal.
example: A manager tracks compliance items and schedules final reviews before submission.

definition: Proposal strategy defines the positioning, evidence and approach used to make a proposal persuasive and competitive.
example: A bidder emphasizes documented reliability because the buyer gives it a high evaluation weight.

definition: A prosecutor's management information system records and organizes information about cases, parties and proceedings for a prosecutorial office.
example: A legal office tracks upcoming hearings and the status of active cases.
sense_note: Could denote the historical PROMIS product or this category of case-management system; verify the named implementation.

definition: Protein characterization uses analytical methods to determine properties of proteins, such as identity, composition, structure or function.
example: A laboratory compares analytical measurements to check whether purified protein samples are consistent.

definition: Protein structure prediction estimates a protein's three-dimensional conformation from its sequence and other available information.
example: A researcher compares candidate structural models to interpret the shape of a protein domain.

definition: Protocol-oriented programming structures software around behavioral interfaces called protocols and types that conform to them.
example: A Swift developer defines a rendering protocol and writes code that accepts multiple conforming types.

definition: Prototype JavaScript Framework is a historical JavaScript library with helpers for DOM operations, events and asynchronous web requests.
example: A legacy page uses Prototype to update a region after a server response.
sense_note: Distinguish the named library from JavaScript's prototype-based object model.

definition: Prototyping creates an early representation of a product or solution to investigate ideas before committing to a full build.
example: A design team tests a clickable mockup to see whether users understand a navigation change.

definition: Protractor was an end-to-end testing framework built on WebDriver for web applications, particularly Angular applications.
example: A team used it to test whether a form submission reached the expected page.
sense_note: Historical framework; do not infer current support.
